title: Avalon FinServ POC — Security Questionnaire Answers & Evidence Index
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures our consolidated responses to Avalon Financial's security questionnaire for the POC, plus an index of supporting evidence artifacts. Scope: Dedicated GPU pool + Private VPC control plane (customer-managed), model serving only for allowed datasets, integration with Avalon's SIEM and KMS. Goal is to provide a single-sheet reference the security/infosec reviewers can use during the workshop and for audit follow-ups.

Customer context:
- Customer: Avalon FinServ (mid-market payments provider)
- POC objective: demonstrate Redwood Private deployed into Avalon's AWS VPC (us-east-1), validate encryption/KMS integration, logging export, and failover behavior under network partition.
- Data: synthetic transaction payloads derived from anonymized sample set; no real PII used in test artifacts.

Workshop summary (Feb 24, 2026):
Attendees: Priya R., Daniel P., Hannah L., Avalon SecOps (Marissa Chen, Omar Basri), Avalon infra (Reza K.), Redwood SRE (Miguel O.).
Key outcomes:
- Confirmed VPC peering + customer-managed NAT gateway pattern for Private control plane access.
- Agreed to rotate test KMS keys after each run and provide audited key usage logs.
- Action: schedule AV/pen test kickoff (defer to legal/contract) — owner: Hannah L., due 2026-03-10.

Questionnaire answers (concise):
1) Data classification & flow
Q: Where does customer data flow?
A: All customer request payloads ingress to the customer's VPC endpoint. For Redwood Private, inference workers run in customer subnet(s) and have no direct egress to the public internet except through customer-managed NATs. Control plane calls (control plane telemetry/health) are routed over mutually authenticated channels to Redwood's control-plane endpoints only if explicitly allowed; otherwise, customer may operate fully air-gapped. Evidence: network diagrams (evidence-01-network-diagram.png).

2) Encryption at rest
Q: How is model and data at rest encrypted?
A: All EBS volumes and object stores used by Redwood workers are encrypted at rest via AWS KMS keys (customer-managed CMKs recommended). Models at rest are stored in encrypted object storage and decrypted in-memory on the worker. Evidence: kms-config-snippet.txt, screenshot of bucket encryption settings.

3) Encryption in transit
Q: TLS and mutual auth?
A: All in-transit communication uses TLS1.3. For Private deployments we support mTLS between control plane components and customers can enable mutual TLS for worker-to-worker and client-to-proxy connections. Evidence: tls-cipher-suite-report.pdf, mTLS-config.md.

4) Key management & HSM
Q: Can Redwood integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, CloudKMS) via key policies and can integrate with HSM-backed key stores for signing and encryption operations. We provide a KMS audit map (evidence-04-kms-audit.csv) showing which resources are encrypted with which key.

5) Access controls & identity
Q: How are identities and roles enforced?
A: Role-based access control (RBAC) in Redwood Console ties to SSO (SAML/OIDC) with SCIM provisioning. Service accounts for workers are separated from human users; secrets injected via KMS/Secrets Manager. We maintain least-privilege IAM policies for platform components. Evidence: scim-config-export.json, rbac-policy-examples.md.

6) Secret handling
Q: How are secrets stored/rotated?
A: Secrets live in customer-managed secrets store or in Redwood's managed vault depending on deployment choice. Rotation policies are configurable with automatic rotation triggers, and we store rotation audit events in Immutable Audit Log (see evidence-07-audit-log-sample.json).

7) Logging & audit
Q: What logs are generated and retained?
A: Detailed request logs, system logs, and audit trails are generated. For Private, logs are streamed to customer SIEM (syslog/forwarder) or to customer-owned S3. Default retention configurable; recommended baseline for Avalon: 365d for high-priority audit logs, 90d for system metrics. Evidence: log-schema.md, sample-cloudtrail-mapping.csv.

8) Monitoring & alerting
Q: Incident detection and alerting?
A: Redwood provides per-route latency/cost SLO alerts and integrates with PagerDuty and customer's Ops channels. For POC we will forward healthcheck alerts to Avalon PagerDuty test integration. Evidence: pd-integration-config.txt.

9) Vulnerability management
Q: How do you handle CVEs and updates?
A: Regular image builds (weekly) with CVE scanning. Critical CVEs trigger emergency builds and out-of-band patches. We provide a CVE tracker extract for all running images in the customer environment. Evidence: cve-tracker-2026-02.csv, base-image-SBoM.txt.

10) Penetration testing
Q: Does Redwood allow customer pen testing against Private deployment?
A: Yes. For hosted deployments we require coordination. For Private deployments within customer VPC, Avalon can run tests against worker instances and network edges following the POC test plan. We require an AUP and scheduled window. Action: Hannah to produce draft AUP by 2026-03-05.

11) Business continuity & DR
Q: RTO/RPO for Dedicated/Private?
A: Dedicated capacity supports regional failover with RTO target of 30 minutes for stateless inference endpoints; RPO varies by customer's cache strategy (we recommend persistent KV backups to S3, replication across AZs). For stateful model sharding, bring-up time is hardware-bound; documented runbooks included. Evidence: dr-runbook.pdf, failover-test-results-2026-02-20.txt.

12) Third-party dependencies
Q: Which third parties process data?
A: For Private deployment under Avalon’s account, third-party exposure limited to software dependencies (OSS libs) and licensing partners (e.g., quantization libraries). We provide a list of critical third-party vendors and their contracts. Evidence: third-party-vendor-list.csv.

13) Privacy & data minimization
Q: How do you prevent retention of sensitive tokens?
A: Redwood supports request redaction rules (pre-tokenization) and on-the-fly anonymization transforms. For the POC, we configured a redaction policy that strips account numbers and full-card PAN patterns before any persistent storage. Evidence: redact-rules.conf, sample-redacted-payloads.json.

Outstanding items and risks:
- Legal acceptance of AUP/pen test window (open). Owner: Hannah L. Target: 2026-03-10.
- Confirm SOC2 scope alignment for Dedicated vs Private prod onboarding. Owner: Sana A. Target: 2026-03-18.
- Validate SIEM field mappings with Avalon's logging team — some custom fields (txn_id, masked_pan) need consistent schemas. Owner: Miguel O. Target: 2026-03-05.
- Hardening checklist to include: enforce MFA on all console logins, service account token TTL reduction to 1h, ensure kubelet TLS bootstrapping is enabled for worker nodes. Owner: Daniel P. Target: 2026-03-08.

Meeting follow-ups and quick wins:
- Deliver condensed "one-page" evidence sheet for Avalon SecOps (2 pages max) — Priya to draft by 2026-03-03.
- Provide sample SIEM ingest mapping file and recommended parsers (Logstash/Fluent) — Miguel to deliver by 2026-03-05.
- Run a focused DR failover rehearsal in staging with Avalon infra — schedule week of 2026-03-15.

Free-form notes (working doc tone):
- Avalon's SecOps asked about removing token content from metrics/observability exports — we should surface which telemetry fields are PII and add a toggle to redact telemetry at source.
- Consider offering a short-term managed HSM option for POC to accelerate sign-off; customer asked for HSM-backed signing logs for regulatory audit.
- Need to patch a minor CVE in the worker image (low severity) before next run; noted in linked CVE tracker.
